title: Finance: Income Tax and Inflation
summary: Using an income tax table with rebates to calculate annual and monthly tax, the tax threshold, and how inflation reduces the value of money over time.

notes.text: Employees pay **income tax** (PAYE) to SARS on their **taxable income**. South Africa uses a **progressive** system: higher income is taxed at a higher rate. Every taxpayer receives a **primary rebate**, an amount subtracted from the tax calculated.

notes.caption: ILLUSTRATIVE tax table for practice (real SARS tables change every year)
rows: R43 200 + 26% of taxable income above R240 000
R78 300 + 31% of taxable income above R375 000
R123 250 + 36% of taxable income above R520 000

notes.text: Illustrative rebates: **primary rebate R17 500** (all taxpayers); secondary rebate R9 500 (65 and older).

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Sizwe (aged 34) has a taxable income of R312 000 per year. Using the illustrative table, calculate his annual and monthly tax.
steps: Subtract primary rebate: R61 920 − R17 500 = R44 420 per year
notes.answer: R44 420 per year; about R3 701,67 per month

notes.text: The income below which no tax is paid, because the tax is less than the rebate. With an 18% rate and a R17 500 rebate: threshold = R17 500 ÷ 0,18 ≈ R97 222.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Tax tables use **annual** income. Convert a monthly salary to an annual one (× 12) first, and divide the final tax by 12 for the monthly amount.
The general increase in prices over time, measured by Stats SA using the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**. If inflation is 5%, an item costing R100 now will cost about R105 next year.

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: A school uniform costs R1 200 now. If inflation averages 6% per year, what will it cost in 3 years?

notes.text: If your salary increases by **less** than inflation, your **buying power** falls: you can afford less than before. Savings should earn interest at a rate above inflation to grow in real terms.

options: higher incomes are taxed at a higher rate

questions.prompt: A monthly taxable salary is R22 500. What is the annual taxable income?
Using the illustrative table, calculate the tax (before rebate) on a taxable income of R180 000.
Using your previous answer, calculate the tax payable after the primary rebate of R17 500.
A loaf of bread costs R18. If inflation is 5%, what will it cost next year? (two decimals)
If your salary increases by 4% while inflation is 6%, your buying power increases.
Ayanda (aged 45) earns a taxable income of R420 000 per year. Using the illustrative table and rebate, calculate her annual tax.
Using your answer above, calculate Ayanda's monthly PAYE.
Explain what the tax threshold is and why a person earning R80 000 a year pays no tax under the illustrative table.
questions.memo:
✓ The income below which no tax is paid (1)
✓ 18% of R80 000 = R14 400, which is less than the R17 500 rebate (1)

questions.prompt: A car service costs R2 500 today. Inflation is expected to be 7% per year. Calculate the cost in 2 years.
